title: Using Boolean Flags instead of Distinct Domain Types
pattern: Using boolean state flags (e.g. `is_quote`, `is_order`) inside a single struct to distinguish between conceptually distinct domain concepts.
why_bad: It violates the Single Responsibility Principle. Different business rules, validation criteria, and states are mixed into a single class, leading to complex nested conditionals.
detection: A single domain struct with multiple optional/nullable fields and boolean flags used to selectively enable or disable attributes.
counterexample: A boolean representing a simple, transient attribute (e.g., `is_active`).
fix: Model the distinct states as separate types or enum variants (e.g., `Quote` and `Order` structs).
